basis: Congenital unilateral enlargement of renal calyces; confined to the kidney.
Micropapillary serous carcinoma denotes an ovarian serous carcinoma pattern; ovarian reproductive tissue has no listed axis.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration defines this ataxia umbrella; extracerebellar organ disease varies across subtypes.
A skeletal dysplasia within chondrodysplasia punctata, affecting bone development.
Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal or neonatal platelets; intracranial hemorrhage is a minority complication.
Postinfectious immune inflammation with characteristic cardiac dysfunction and shock; other organ injuries vary, and GI symptoms alone do not establish damage.
Inherited prion disease causes progressive cerebral degeneration and cognitive impairment; prion disease belongs to the transmissible infectious mechanism axis.
Isolated inherited hair-shaft disorder with woolly, sparse and fragile hair.
Cancer originates in the tonsillar pillar of the oropharynx, which belongs to the upper-airway axis.
Congenital absence of the foot is a skeletal developmental defect.
Skeletal dysplasia and abnormal skin define this glycosylation disorder; blue sclerae/proptosis do not establish ocular damage; aortopathy is not established at 30%.
Malignant tumour of lymphatic vascular endothelium; cutaneous location is not specified for the umbrella concept.
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Enteropathy, immunodeficiency and hepatic fibrosis (14/27); neurodevelopmental delay 10/16. Hair-shaft abnormalities (22/22) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Germ-cell tumour arising in the adult central nervous system.
Treponemal bacterial infection umbrella; persistent damage to a particular organ is not shared across most patients.
Cold-reacting autoantibodies cause intravascular red-cell destruction; hemoglobinuria alone does not establish renal damage.
Congenital absence of both upper limbs is a limb skeletal developmental defect.
Abnormal ocular drainage causes elevated intraocular pressure, corneal changes and optic-nerve damage.
Cardiomyopathy and hearing loss define the syndrome; accompanying myopathy and ataxia have no established frequency of at least 30%.
Refsum-spectrum alpha-oxidation defects cause retinopathy (~100%), neuropathy (~70%) and hearing loss (~60%); ichthyosis omitted under the cap.
Diffuse cerebral degeneration causes dementia and spastic paraplegia; hearing impairment and blindness lack frequency and localization evidence.
Skin/nail changes and diagnostic oral leukoplakia (40%); IgA deficiency 44% and recurrent infections 30% support immunodeficiency. Anemia occurs in only 10%.
Spastic paraplegia with neurodevelopmental impairment; reduced visual acuity occurs in 2/4, with retinal abnormalities. Hearing loss and cleft palate each occur in 1/4.
Asymptomatic persistent Treponema pallidum infection; later symptomatic organ disease is a separate stage and is not labelled here.
